label: What is its own being lacks no perfection of being, being in act in it formally or eminently
paraphrase: The formal-or-eminent reading of ST I q.4 a.2 ad 3's reason clause ('nulla de perfectionibus essendi potest deesse ei quod est ipsum esse subsistens'): whatever is its own being is in act, in the frame's mode-open act, in every perfection of being. 'Not lacking' is read as being in act formally or eminently, the HAVING_EVERY_PERFECTION_1 side of DISAMB dc9c0a1b, not as really having the perfection as a determination (d164b1ff, the HAVING_EVERY_PERFECTION_2 side). The same article satisfies 'not lacking' through eminent preexistence (first proof) and 'ut unum' (ad 1). Sibling reading, not a strength-ordered version: no statement relates InAct to Has.
